# NSQD, Necessity Squared

> Bespoke fabrication and brand activation studio operating from Jebel Ali
> in Dubai and Wynberg in Cape Town. End-to-end production, or by-the-part
> manufacturing for designers, brands, and creative production houses.

NSQD designs, fabricates, and installs physical objects at scale: brand
activations, theatrical scale props, scale models, retail kits, trophies,
production runs, and bespoke commissions. Two cities, one team.

## What NSQD does

NSQD operates a fully equipped fabrication workshop with the following
production capabilities:

- CO2 laser cutting (acrylic, MDF, paper, fabric)
- Fiber laser cutting (stainless steel, aluminium, brass)
- UV flatbed printing (direct-to-rigid substrate, 4x8 ft bed)
- ECO solvent large-format printing (vinyl, banner, textile)
- DTF (direct-to-film) textile transfer
- 3D printing (FDM, SLA, resin finishing)
- CAD/CAM design and production engineering
- Assembly and on-site installation (UAE and South Africa)

Two buyer paths:
- End-to-end: turnkey project from brief to install
- By the part: quoted production for clients with a shopping list

## Selected work

- 1Rebel: interactive prize wheel for a fitness pop-up (CO2 laser plus UV
  flatbed, 14 days brief-to-opening)
- IDEX Display: APC scale model for institutional display (large-format
  SLA 3D-print plus hand-finishing, 6 weeks)
- People & Co: multi-year production partnership covering Union Day 2023
  diorama boxes, Eid Al Etihad 2024 large-scale palm fronds, and the
  Natural History Museum 2026 ember props for live broadcast
- NYU Abu Dhabi: institutional basketball trophy (SLA plus hand-finishing)
- Graff: bamboo fan and velvet-pouch kit for a brand activation
  (Pantone-matched, hand-engraved)

## Markets served

- UAE and the wider GCC, from the Dubai workshop
- South Africa, nationwide, from the Cape Town studio
- UK and EU agencies producing events in the GCC, built locally in Dubai

- Cape Town: Wynberg, South Africa (studio plus installation team)

## Brand and tone

NSQD's voice is workshop-first: confident, not corporate. The studio
emphasises what's visible on the floor: materials, machines, kerf
edges, build photos, named brands, named numbers, named deadlines.
Adverts and agency-speak are explicitly avoided.
